items.summary: Add a 'Timeframe' selector to the Trade Entry Checker form with options: 1m, 15m, and 1h. Default the selection to 1m (the user's most-used timeframe). Display the selector prominently near the top of the form, before the indicator inputs.

When the selected timeframe is 1m, replace the EMA20/EMA50/EMA200 inputs with EMA9 and EMA21 inputs (as these are the relevant fast EMAs for 1-minute charts). Hide the EMA200 field for 1m. Show EMA20, EMA50, EMA200 for 15m and 1h timeframes. Update all field labels accordingly.

For the 1m timeframe, remove the MACD Direction input from the Trade Entry Checker form, as MACD is not recommended for 1-minute charts (too slow, too noisy). Display a short informational note explaining this omission (e.g., 'MACD is not recommended for 1m charts due to excessive noise.'). For 15m and 1h, keep the MACD Direction dropdown.

Adapt the ATR interpretation hint shown in the Trade Entry Checker form based on the selected timeframe. For 1m: show a note that ATR on 1m is only useful as an activity filter (not for SL/TP calculation) and is optional. For 15m and 1h: keep the standard ATR description. The ATR input field should be marked as optional for 1m and required for 15m/1h.

Update the rule engine in tradeEntryRules.ts (or equivalent) to evaluate conditions based on the selected timeframe. For 1m: evaluate (1) EMA9 > EMA21 alignment (Long) or EMA9 < EMA21 (Short); (2) Price proximity: current price within 1× ATR of EMA9 (if ATR provided), else skip the proximity check; (3) RSI extremes use tighter thresholds: RSI < 75 for Long (not overbought), RSI > 25 for Short (not oversold). MACD condition is omitted for 1m. For 15m: use EMA20/EMA50/EMA200 alignment, RSI thresholds < 65 / > 35, and MACD as before. For 1h: same as 15m.

Display the selected timeframe in the Trade Entry Checker results summary card (alongside the asset name and trade direction badge), so the user always sees which timeframe the verdict was calculated for.
